analysis: Examined the base text of .github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py (lines 1-840) together with the complete patch (range_map_complete=true). The change is confined to WorkflowBoundaryTests.test_secret_bearing_workflow_separates_current_scanner_from_pinned_base_context. Head lines 743 and 752-761 change the asserted workflow text in five ways. (1) THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA now comes only from github.event.pull_request.base.sha; the env fallback is removed. (2) timeout-minutes rises from 20 to 60, and THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is set to 3000. (3) Bedrock call and token budgets are added: a workload policy, 500 max workload calls and 16384 max output tokens by default, each overridable through repo vars. BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS must be absent. (4) The review job must not reference workflow_dispatch, pr_number or review_depth. (5) The existing pull_request_target, default-branch scanner checkout, no head.sha/head.ref, persist-credentials:false and hash-pinned pip assertions remain. Taken together, these tightenings reduce manual-dispatch attack surface and keep fork head content as data. This is CI test tooling and does not touch the provider, coordinator or native runtime assets in the threat model (A-001..A-017, TB-002/003/007/009/010/011, T-041 and others). No canonical threat applies, and no regression was identified. The tests constrain workflow text but do not prove the actual .github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml, which was not supplied. Integration should confirm that the workflow matches these assertions. In particular, it should check that removing workflow_dispatch does not leave other triggers with secret access to untrusted refs. It should also check that the repo-var-controlled budget values cannot be set by PR authors; repo vars are maintainer-controlled. A longer timeout affects only CI cost and availability.
